prompt: Why is Vitest the natural runner for the planner?

choices.text: It is the only runner that supports TypeScript at all
choices.why: Jest runs TypeScript too, with a transformer.

choices.text: It reads the project's own Vite setup
choices.why: Right. Nothing else to configure.

choices.text: It starts a real browser for every test file it finds
choices.why: It runs in Node; jsdom is a simulated document.

choices.text: Vite refuses to build without it
choices.why: The build does not depend on any test runner.

prompt: `npm test` with no test files at all exits with code 1. Why is that the right default?

choices.text: Because exit code 1 means the run was skipped
choices.why: Any non-zero code means failure to whoever runs it.

choices.text: Because Vitest needs at least one test to load jsdom
choices.why: jsdom has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: A typo in a file name must not look like a green suite
choices.why: Right. Finding nothing is reported as a failure.

choices.text: It is not right; it is a bug
choices.why: It is deliberate, and the lesson argues for it.

prompt: Why does the weekOf test use `toEqual` rather than `toBe`?

choices.text: Two arrays with the same items are still two arrays
choices.why: Right. `toBe` is `===`, and `toEqual` compares contents.

choices.text: `toBe` only works on strings
choices.why: It works on numbers too; the totals use it.

choices.text: `toEqual` ignores the order of the dates in the array
choices.why: Order matters to it.

choices.text: `toBe` is slower on arrays
choices.why: Speed is not the difference; the answer is.

prompt: The lesson says to work the expected value out by hand. What goes wrong if you copy it from what the code printed?

choices.text: The test fails the first time it runs
choices.why: It passes, which is the problem.

choices.text: The test only checks that the code agrees with itself
choices.why: Right. Copied from the buggy weekOf, 155 would have been green.

choices.text: Vitest refuses expected values that came from the console
choices.why: It cannot know where a number came from.

choices.text: Nothing; it is a faster way to the same test
choices.why: It is a different test: one that cannot find this bug.

prompt: Why did the test of the JavaScript total pass before the fix?

choices.text: JavaScript sessions are stored in UTC
choices.why: Every session is stored the same way.

choices.text: The filter by course runs before the week is computed
choices.why: Order does not matter here; both filters run.

choices.text: Vitest skips the second test in a describe
choices.why: It ran and passed.

choices.text: Its sessions sit inside both weeks
choices.why: Right. It passed by luck, which is why the edges need sessions.

prompt: What does `new Date("2026-10-21")` mean?

choices.text: Midnight on the 21st where the computer is
choices.why: That is what most people expect, and it is the bug.

choices.text: Midnight on the 21st in UTC
choices.why: Right. A date with no time is read as UTC.

choices.text: Noon on the 21st, to stay clear of both midnights
choices.why: No such rule exists in JavaScript.

choices.text: An invalid date, because it has no time
choices.why: It is valid; it means UTC midnight.

prompt: A developer in Lisbon runs the original weekOf test and sees it pass. What does that show?

choices.text: That the bug is in Vitest's handling of São Paulo
choices.why: Vitest only reports what weekOf returned.

choices.text: That the code is correct and the São Paulo machine misconfigured
choices.why: Both machines are configured correctly; the code depends on the zone.

choices.text: That a test tied to the machine's zone answers per machine
choices.why: Right. The zone you work in is the one where your mistakes do not show.

choices.text: Nothing; Lisbon and UTC are never the same
choices.why: Lisbon is on UTC for half the year.

prompt: The fix replaces `getDay` and `setDate` with `getUTCDay` and ___ .
After the fix, why does `today()` still use the local `getDate()`?

choices.text: A student's today is the date on their own wall
choices.why: Right. That one must follow the local calendar.

choices.text: Because it was forgotten in the fix
choices.why: It is deliberate, and a test pins it.

choices.text: UTC methods do not exist for the current date
choices.why: They do; `getUTCDate` works on any date.

choices.text: Because `today()` is never tested, so it does not matter
choices.why: It is tested, with a stopped clock.

prompt: Why are 0 and 601 the values tested for minutes, rather than 300?

choices.text: Because 300 is too large for jsdom
choices.why: These are unit tests; no jsdom is involved.

choices.text: Just outside each boundary is where an off-by-one shows
choices.why: Right. A value in the middle finds nothing.

choices.text: Because `addSession` accepts every value between them
choices.why: It refuses 2.5, which is between them.

choices.text: Because the form cannot send any other number
choices.why: It can send any number at all.

prompt: What does `%s` do in the name of a `test.each`?

choices.text: It marks the test as skipped
choices.why: Skipping is `test.skip`.

choices.text: It makes the test run in a separate process
choices.why: Nothing about processes changes.

choices.text: It puts the value in the test's name
choices.why: Right. Each case fails on its own line.

choices.text: It formats the value as a date
choices.why: It prints it as text, whatever it is.

choices.text: The number of calls to `addSession`

choices.text: The file `courses.json` before and after

choices.text: Nothing: comments are ignored by every tool

prompt: Why does the course pin jsdom at 29.1.1 rather than 30?

choices.text: `setSystemTime` fails without it
